q: A patient with advanced illness experiences dyspnea. According to Hazzard, how should nonpharmacologic measures be incorporated into symptom management?
o: Include them from the outset alongside an appropriate pharmacologic approach
Defer them until the available pharmacologic treatments have been exhausted
Use them in place of assessment and treatment of the underlying cause
Prefer supplemental oxygen to them when there is no evidence of hypoxia
explanation:
**Start nonpharmacologic measures alongside appropriate medication** for dyspnea in advanced illness. Upright positioning, airflow across the face and breathing techniques can reduce distress while reversible causes are assessed.

**A. Include measures from the outset.** They can be implemented promptly and used with disease-directed or palliative treatments.
**B. Wait for all medicines to fail.** This unnecessarily delays a low-burden source of relief.
**C. Replace etiologic assessment.** Treatable contributors such as fluid overload, infection or bronchospasm still warrant attention.
**D. Prefer oxygen without hypoxemia.** A fan or airflow may help a nonhypoxemic patient. Oxygen is particularly useful when hypoxemia is present.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 69, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

. Wait for all medicines to fail.** This unnecessarily delays a low-burden source of relief.
. Replace etiologic assessment.** Treatable contributors such as fluid overload, infection or bronchospasm still warrant attention.
. Prefer oxygen without hypoxemia.** A fan or airflow may help a nonhypoxemic patient. Oxygen is particularly useful when hypoxemia is present.

explanationParts.text: **Start nonpharmacologic measures alongside appropriate medication** for dyspnea in advanced illness. Upright positioning, airflow across the face and breathing techniques can reduce distress while reversible causes are assessed.

q: אישה כתבה הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות. כעת היא סובלת מקושי בבליעה, אך לא נקבע שהיא חולה הנוטה למות או שאינה בעלת כשרות. מה יש לברר לפני החלת ההנחיות כמסלול ההחלטה לפי חוק זה?
o: האם בני המשפחה מעדיפים את הטיפול המוצע כעת
האם מתקיימים תנאי תחולת החוק וההנחיות
האם עצם קושי הבליעה מספיק להפעלת ההנחיות
האם אבחנת דמנציה מחליפה קביעת מצב וכשרות
explanation:
הנחיות מקדימות מכוח חוק החולה הנוטה למות נועדו לנסיבות מוגדרות. בודקים אם נקבע שהאדם נוטה למות ואינו בעל כשרות ואם ההוראה תקפה ורלוונטית. **האם מתקיימים תנאי תחולת החוק וההנחיות**.

**א. האם בני המשפחה מעדיפים את הטיפול המוצע כעת.** רצון הקרובים אינו קובע את תחולת המסמך.
**ב. האם מתקיימים תנאי תחולת החוק וההנחיות.** מעמד החולה ותוכן ההוראה נבחנים לפני יישומה.
**ג. האם עצם קושי הבליעה מספיק להפעלת ההנחיות.** דיספגיה כשלעצמה אינה קביעה לפי החוק.
**ד. האם אבחנת דמנציה מחליפה קביעת מצב וכשרות.** דמנציה אינה שקולה לאובדן כשרות או לקביעה פרוגנוסטית.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס״ו-2005, עמ׳ 16.

q: A 72-year-old woman hospitalized for a severe COPD exacerbation develops new urinary incontinence and delirium after previously living independently and remaining continent. She receives prednisone, ipratropium, levofloxacin, and recently added tolterodine. Her vital signs are normal, her CAM screen is positive, and postvoid residual urine is elevated. Which approach addresses a potentially reversible medication contribution while providing toileting assistance?
o: Withdraw tolterodine and provide scheduled assistance with toileting
Increase tolterodine and provide scheduled assistance with toileting
Continue tolterodine and wait for the patient to request toileting
Continue tolterodine and reduce the frequency of toileting assistance
explanation:
Acute illness, delirium and drugs can turn a previously continent patient into someone unable to reach the toilet or empty the bladder. **Withdraw tolterodine, assist with scheduled toileting and reassess the elevated residual.**

**A. Withdraw tolterodine and provide scheduled assistance with toileting** — This addresses the antimuscarinic contribution and the immediate cognitive barrier to toileting.
**B. Increase tolterodine and provide scheduled assistance with toileting** — Escalating tolterodine may further impair bladder contraction and cognition.
**C. Continue tolterodine and wait for the patient to request toileting** — A delirious patient may neither recognize urgency nor request help in time.
**D. Continue tolterodine and reduce the frequency of toileting assistance** — Less assistance increases opportunities for leakage while the medication continues to impede emptying.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, pp. 701–704, 711–714.

optionRationales.body: . Withdraw tolterodine and provide scheduled assistance with toileting** — This addresses the antimuscarinic contribution and the immediate cognitive barrier to toileting.
. Increase tolterodine and provide scheduled assistance with toileting** — Escalating tolterodine may further impair bladder contraction and cognition.
. Continue tolterodine and wait for the patient to request toileting** — A delirious patient may neither recognize urgency nor request help in time.
. Continue tolterodine and reduce the frequency of toileting assistance** — Less assistance increases opportunities for leakage while the medication continues to impede emptying.

explanationParts.text: Acute illness, delirium and drugs can turn a previously continent patient into someone unable to reach the toilet or empty the bladder. **Withdraw tolterodine, assist with scheduled toileting and reassess the elevated residual.**

q: An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer dementia has become more confused over three days. He lives in assisted living and has a baseline MMSE of 19/30. He accused staff of stealing a wallet later found in his drawer and now reports seeing children who are not present. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Temperature is 36.8 degrees C, BP 140/85, and heart rate 78; urine shows 10-20 white cells and positive nitrites. Which feature most strongly supports delirium superimposed on his baseline dementia?
o: The visual hallucinations.
The paranoid interpretations.
The abrupt change over three days.
The abnormal urinalysis.
explanation:
Delusions and visual hallucinations can occur with either a chronic neurocognitive disorder or delirium. The patient's prior state and speed of change distinguish the new episode.
**Onset over three days is the strongest clue to delirium superimposed on his dementia.**

**A. The visual hallucinations** — Visual hallucinations alone cannot date the change or identify its cause.
**B. The paranoid interpretations** — Paranoid beliefs occur in dementia as well as delirium.
**C. The abrupt change over three days** — The departure from his usual state over a few days warrants attention testing and medical evaluation.
**D. The abnormal urinalysis** — Urine abnormalities may prompt further clinical assessment but do not define a cognitive syndrome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 883, 885–886

. The paranoid interpretations** — Paranoid beliefs occur in dementia as well as delirium.
. The abrupt change over three days** — The departure from his usual state over a few days warrants attention testing and medical evaluation.
. The abnormal urinalysis** — Urine abnormalities may prompt further clinical assessment but do not define a cognitive syndrome.

**Onset over three days is the strongest clue to delirium superimposed on his dementia.**

q: A 78-year-old man with metastatic cancer and uncontrolled pain says that he wants to die and that he has a gun. A suicidal plan and intent have not yet been assessed. Which action is needed now alongside treatment of his suffering?
o: Adjust analgesia and revisit the statement at the next appointment
Start an antidepressant and reassess after its therapeutic effect
Assess a suicide plan and reduce access to the firearm
Discuss treatment goals and arrange routine outpatient follow-up
explanation:
A patient with advanced cancer can need relief from suffering and immediate suicide-risk assessment at the same time. Uncontrolled pain and ready access to lethal means increase concern.
**Assess intent, plan and immediate safety now, and arrange to reduce access to the firearm.**

**A. Adjust analgesia and wait.** Treat pain promptly. Delaying assessment leaves a potentially imminent risk unexplored.
**B. Start an antidepressant and wait.** Antidepressants generally take weeks to have a measurable effect and do not secure the environment today.
**C. Assess the plan and reduce access.** Ask directly, involve appropriate supports to secure the environment and arrange emergency evaluation if danger is imminent.
**D. Discuss goals at routine follow-up.** Goals of care deserve attention now, alongside safety and symptom control. Routine follow-up alone is inadequate.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1013, 1017–1018

. Start an antidepressant and wait.** Antidepressants generally take weeks to have a measurable effect and do not secure the environment today.
. Assess the plan and reduce access.** Ask directly, involve appropriate supports to secure the environment and arrange emergency evaluation if danger is imminent.
. Discuss goals at routine follow-up.** Goals of care deserve attention now, alongside safety and symptom control. Routine follow-up alone is inadequate.

q: מה מהווה מרכיב של המדד הפרוגנוסטי (IPSS) ב- MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROME ?
o: נוכחות B SYMPTOMS
ערך של LDH מעל 600
גיל מעל 75
נויטרופילים מתחת ל- 800
explanation:
The revised MDS score grades marrow blasts, cytogenetic risk and the depth of three cytopenias. **An absolute neutrophil count below 800 per microliter contributes to IPSS-R.** The original IPSS counts cytopenic lineages, using 1,800 neutrophils per microliter as the cutoff for neutropenia. IPSS-R separately scores neutrophils below 800.

**A. B symptoms** — Fever, drenching sweats and weight loss are familiar lymphoma features and do not contribute points to IPSS-R.
**B. LDH above 600** — This enzyme is not one of the five core IPSS-R variables.
**C. Age over 75** — Age influences survival and treatment decisions, but this cutoff is not a core IPSS-R scoring variable.
**D. Neutrophils below 800** — An absolute count below 0.8 billion per liter earns half a point in the revised system.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1484–1485, Table 95-1; Greenberg et al., Blood 2012, Table 3, and Blood 1998;91:1100, correction to the original IPSS.

Key note: The question names the original IPSS, but the 800-per-microliter threshold belongs to IPSS-R. Hazzard Table 95-1 also prints 0.8 beside a cells-per-microliter label. The IPSS-R unit is billions per liter.
